mission_06: You have extended MAML to few-shot classification, the setting where it has had the most impact. The cross-entropy loss with softmax is the standard for classification, and its gradient (softmax output minus one-hot label) is both elegant and computationally efficient. The N-way K-shot evaluation protocol simulates the real-world scenario of learning new categories from few examples. MAML's model-agnostic nature means this approach works with any differentiable classifier — from simple linear models to deep convolutional networks. On benchmarks like miniImageNet, MAML achieves strong few-shot classification performance by learning an initialization that captures transferable visual features. The key insight remains: optimize for adaptability, not just performance.
